1: # Job Post Editor — Fields & Entity Alignment
2: 
3: Reference for the **Job Post Builder** in Recruitment Management: what each
4: field is, where its value comes from, and which database entity owns it.
5: 
6: - Frontend: `frontend/src/components/modules/RecruitmentManagement.tsx`
7: - Backend: `backend-laravel/Modules/RecruitmentManagement/`
8: - Core HCM source: `backend-laravel/Modules/CoreHCM/`
9: 
10: ---
11: 
12: ## 1. Field ownership at a glance
13: 
14: Every Job Info field resolves to exactly one owning entity. Nothing is typed
15: twice: the builder reads Core HCM and writes only the recruitment-side record.
16: 
17: | Builder field | Reads from | Written to | Auto? |
18: |---|---|---|---|
19: | Title | `positions.title` | derived on save | auto |
20: | Department | `departments.name` | `job_posts.department_id` | selected |
21: | Type | — | `job_posts.employment_type` | manual |
22: | Schedule | — | `job_posts.schedule` | selected |
23: | **Vacancies** | `requisitions.requested_count`, else `positions.headcount − filled_count` | `job_posts.vacancies` | **auto** |
24: | **Salary min** | `salary_grades.min_salary` via position's band | `job_posts.salary_min` | **auto** |
25: | **Salary max** | `salary_grades.max_salary` via position's band | `job_posts.salary_max` | **auto** |
26: | Education level | requirement templates | `job_posts.education_level` | selected |
27: | Experience level | requirement templates | `job_posts.experience_level` | selected |
28: | Description / Responsibilities / Qualifications / Skills / Instructions / About | AI draft or manual | `*_json` columns | manual / AI |
29: | Picture of hiring | upload | `job_posts.picture` | manual |
30: 
31: ---
32: 
33: ## 2. Entity relationship
34: 
35: ```
36: departments ──1:N──> positions ──1:N──> job_posts ──1:N──> applicants
37:       │                    │                 │
38:       │                    │                 └──> job_post_platforms (Website/Facebook/Instagram/Indeed)
39:       │                    │
40:       │                    ├──N:1──> salary_grades   (the band: min_salary / max_salary)
41:       │                    │                 │
42:       │                    │                 └──> source of Salary min / max
43:       │                    │
44:       │                    └── headcount / filled_count  (source of Vacancies)
45:       │
46:       └── name (label shown in the builder)
47: 
48: requisitions ──> departments + positions      (requested_count → Vacancies)
49:       │
50:       └── converted_job_post_id ──> job_posts  (Pending → Done → Converted)
51: ```
52: 
53: ### Ownership rules
54: 
55: | Entity | Owns | Never stores |
56: |---|---|---|
57: | `departments` | name, code, head | vacancy counts |
58: | `positions` | title, headcount, filled_count, salary_grade_id | posting text, published status |
59: | `salary_grades` | code, title, min_salary, max_salary, level | which post uses it |
60: | `requisitions` | requested_count, urgency, justification, status | salary, published content |
61: | `job_posts` | the published ad: salary, vacancies, content, platforms | headcount (lives on the position) |
62: 
63: `positions.headcount − positions.filled_count` is the **open slots** figure.
64: `PositionResource` already exposes it as a computed `vacancies` field, so no
65: extra column is required.
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 3. Auto-filled fields
70: 
71: ### 3.1 Salary min / max
72: 
73: The band is resolved from Core HCM and written straight into the two inputs.
74: No grade selector, no "apply" button.
75: 
76: ```
77: positions.salary_grade_id ──> salary_grades ──> min_salary / max_salary
78:                                                      │
79:                                                      ▼
80:                                         Salary min (₱) / Salary max (₱)
81: ```
82: 
83: Resolution order for the band:
84: 
85: 1. `draft.salaryGradeId` (set when a position is chosen)
86: 2. `draftPosition.salaryGradeId` — the position's assigned grade
87: 3. `draftPosition.salaryGradeMin/Max` — band values already resolved on load
88: 
89: Behaviour:
90: 
91: - Picking a position or linking a requisition fills both fields automatically.
92: - Typing a figure sets `salaryLocked` — your number is then preserved.
93: - Changing the position/grade re-arms the sync (`bandSourceRef`), refilling both.
94: - **Reset to band** appears under Salary max only while `salaryLocked` is true;
95:   it clears the lock and restores the Core HCM figures.
96: - `Edit Template` starts locked so an already-published post's live salary is
97:   never silently rewritten.
98: 
99: ### 3.2 Vacancies
100: 
101: Priority order:
102: 
103: | # | Source | Value | Label shown to HR |
104: |---|--------|-------|-------------------|
105: | 1 | Linked requisition | `requested_count` | requisition `REQ-00007` |
106: | 2 | Core HCM position | `headcount − filled_count` | open slots |
107: | 3 | Neither | `1` | — |
108: 
109: - Floor of **1**: a fully-staffed position still needs a posting.
110: - Floor of **filled**: a post can never advertise fewer slots than the hires it
111:   already recorded.
112: - Editing the field sets `vacanciesLocked`; **Reset vacancies** restores the
113:   Core HCM figure.
114: - Changing the position or requisition re-arms the sync automatically
115:   (`vacancySourceRef`).
116: - Admins converting from a requisition get the input `disabled` — the requested
117:   count is authoritative and must not be hand-edited.
118: 
119: ---
120: 
121: ## 4. Editor flow
122: 
123: ```
124:                     ┌──────────────────────────────┐
125:   New post ─────────>│                              │
126:   Copy & Use ──────>│      JOB POST BUILDER        │──> Save draft ──> status: Draft
127:   Convert req ─────>│   (9 draggable content       │                  active: false
128:   Edit Template ───>│    blocks + Job Info)        │──> Publish  ───> status: Open
129:                     │                              │                  active: true
130:                     └──────────────────────────────┘
131: ```
132: 
133: ### Entry points and their seeding
134: 
135: | Entry | `editingJobId` | Salary | Vacancies |
136: |---|---|---|---|
137: | **New post** | `null` | auto from band | auto from position |
138: | **Copy & Use Template** | `null` | auto (unlocked) | auto (unlocked) |
139: | **Convert requisition** | `null` | auto from band | requested count, locked for admins |
140: | **Edit Template** | job id | **locked** — keeps published values | **locked** — keeps published values |
141: | **Link pending request** | unchanged | re-armed | re-armed |
142: 
143: ### The 9 blocks
144: 
145: | Block | Content |
146: |---|---|
147: | `title` | Position + department pickers |
148: | `info` | Type, schedule, vacancies, salary min/max, education, experience |
149: | `description` | Job description |
150: | `responsibilities` | Key responsibilities |
151: | `qualifications` | Qualifications |
152: | `skills` | Required skills |
153: | `instructions` | Application instructions |
154: | `about` | About the company |
155: | `picture` | Hiring poster upload |
156: 
157: Publishing requires title, department, and all six text blocks. Missing blocks
158: are added to the canvas automatically and focus moves to the first one.
159: 
160: ---
161: 
162: ## 5. Server-side behaviour
163: 
164: `RecruitmentManagementController`:
165: 
166: | Concern | Behaviour |
167: |---|---|
168: | Salary defaulting | `applyPositionSalaryDefaults()` fills blank `salary_min`/`salary_max` from the position's grade — called in **both** `store()` and `update()` |
169: | Title / slug | Derived from the linked position by the `JobPost` model, so a post can never drift from its position |
170: | Duplicate guard | One posting per position + department; `POST` → 409 `DUPLICATE_JOB_POST` with `existing_job_post_id`; `PUT` only 409s when the pair genuinely changes |
171: | Poster serving | `GET /job-posts/{id}/picture` tries several legacy paths, falls back to the composed template poster, never 404s |
172: | Vacancy lifecycle | `fillOneSlot()` increments `filled_count` and auto-closes the post at 0 slots |
173: | Position creation | `StorePositionRequest` requires `salary_grade_id` and `headcount ≥ 1` |
174: 
175: ---
176: 
177: ## 6. Known gaps
178: 
179: | Gap | Impact |
180: |---|---|
181: | `job_posts.vacancies` is never validated against `positions.headcount` | A post can advertise more slots than HR approved |
182: | `UpdateJobPostRequest` drops the `gte:salary_min` check that `StoreJobPostRequest` has | An edit can save `salary_max < salary_min` |
183: | Salary band can only be changed in Core HCM, not the builder | Recruiters must leave the job post screen to move a role to another band |
184: | A stale duplicate `JobPost` model exists at `backend-laravel/app/Models/JobPost.php` | Missing `requires_practical` / `picture`; the module model is the one controllers use |
185: | The `info` block is ~200 lines of JSX inside an 8,000-line file | Candidate for extraction into a `JobInfoPanel` component |

**`job_posts.skills_json` is the ONLY source of `required_skills` in the entire screening pipeline.** If the user removes the Required Skills block, `buildRequirements()` returns `required_skills => []`, which means:

- `buildOpenJobs()` filter would exclude posts with no skills/certs/education/experience
- The coverage gate `required_skills_coverage_min` becomes meaningless
- Skills recognition → 0

```
Job Post Builder (draft.skills, qualifications, educationLevel, experienceLevel)

ScreeningService::buildRequirements(JobPost)

ApplicantScreening + applicants.status/fit_score

# Skill: browser-automation # browser-automation Closes the edit → run → **look at it** → fix loop that otherwise requires the user to describe what is on their screen. ## Usage ```bash node /browser.mjs [options] ``` `` is the folder you just read this file from — `browser.mjs` sits beside it. Use that path literally rather than guessing at a home directory. | option | meaning | |---|---| | `--snapshot` | list every interactive element with a clickable ref (add `--full` for the whole accessibility tree) | | `--wait ` | block until the selector appears (default: DOM ready) | | `--eval ` | run an expression in the page, print the JSON result | | `--script ` | drive a sequence — see **Scripting** below | | `--screenshot

` | write a PNG — read it afterwards to look at it | | `--timeout ` | navigation timeout, default 30000 | | `--session ` | keep ONE page alive across calls — see **Sessions** below | | `--close` | with `--session `, tear that session's browser down | ## Driving by ref, not by selector `--snapshot` returns the page's interactive elements, each with a ref: ``` @e5 button "Audit my code" @e9 button "Select your model" [haspopup=menu] @e10 button "Manual" [haspopup=menu] @e11 button "Send" [disabled] ``` Click `@e10` and you get what the page says is there — no selector to author from a DOM you cannot see. This matters most for **icon-only buttons**, which have no accessible name at all: `getByRole('button', {name: …})` cannot find them, and they show up here as `@e1 button [haspopup=dialog]`. A ref is stamped into the page, so it dies on navigation or a re-render. **Re-snapshot after anything that changes the page** — the refs renumber, and a stale one matches nothing. `--full` returns the accessibility tree instead (headings, text, links). Use refs to *act*, `--full` to *read*. ## Scripting a sequence `--script` runs a file that default-exports `async (page, ui) => result`. **`page` is a Playwright `Page`** (the driver is patchright, a Playwright fork), so use the Playwright API — `page.locator`, `page.getByRole`, `page.getByText`, `page.waitForFunction`, `page.evaluate`. It is NOT Puppeteer: `page.$` and friends mostly work, but `getByRole` and `locator` do not exist there, so code written against Puppeteer will fail in confusing ways. **`ui` is the ref helper**, and is usually the shorter path: | call | does | |---|---| | `await ui.snapshot()` | the ref listing above, as a string | | `await ui.snapshot({full: true})` | the accessibility tree instead | | `await ui.click('@e7')` | click that element | | `await ui.fill('@e3', 'text')` | fill an input | | `await ui.text('@e5')` | its inner text | | `ui.ref('@e5')` | the raw locator, for anything else | Whatever you return is printed as JSON. The runner owns the browser, the console/network capture and the teardown; the script only drives and asserts. ```js // qa.mjs — node /browser.mjs http://localhost:3000 --script ./qa.mjs export default async function run(page, ui) { // Look at what is there before deciding what to click. const before = await ui.snapshot() const signIn = before.match(/@(e\d+) button "Sign in"/)?.[1] if (!signIn) return { error: 'no sign-in button', snapshot: before } await ui.click(signIn) await page.waitForTimeout(500) // The page changed, so the old refs are gone — snapshot again. const after = await ui.snapshot() return { opened: after.includes('textbox'), after } } ``` Navigation to the URL argument has already happened before your function runs. You can navigate further with `page.goto(...)`. ## Read the text before the pixels `--screenshot` writes a PNG and **you can read it** — a read of an image returns the picture. If it comes back as `[binary file: png …]` this host has no image path; say so rather than guessing at what rendered. Even so, reach for text first. It is not just cheaper — it is more precise: - `--snapshot` — every interactive element, with refs - `--snapshot --full` — the accessibility tree: headings, text, links - `--eval "…"` — ask the DOM a direct question - the console/network report, which catches most breakage for almost nothing A screenshot costs tens of thousands of tokens and answers "does this look right", which is a narrower question than it seems. Use it for layout and visual regressions, and use the tree for everything about structure, content and state. ## Interpreting the report - `console.error` / uncaught exceptions → almost always a real bug. - `requests failed` → a 404 on a JS chunk usually means a stale build is being served; a 500 means the server, not the page. - `title` empty and `bodyChars` near zero → the app did not mount at all. Check the console section first, not the DOM. ## Examples ```bash # Did my change render? node /browser.mjs http://localhost:3000 # Assert something specific about the DOM node /browser.mjs http://localhost:3000 \ --eval "document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid=row]').length" # Wait for a late-mounting element before judging the page node /browser.mjs http://localhost:3000 --wait "[data-testid=grid]" ``` ## Gotchas found by using this - **Keep the trailing slash** on a path-prefixed app. `http://host/app` and `http://host/app/` resolve relative asset URLs differently, and without it a page can return HTTP 200 with `bodyChars 0` and never mount. An app that 200s but renders nothing is usually this, not a crash. - **A failing request is not automatically a bug.** Apps routinely probe for optional local services that are simply not running. Check whether the dependency is meant to exist before reporting it. - **Never assert on text your own input put on the page.** A check for "console error" matches the prompt you just typed into the app as readily as the thing you were looking for, and the test passes while proving nothing. Match only strings that can come from the system under test. - **Wait for content, not for a fixed delay.** A client-rendered app that is merely slow is indistinguishable from one that is broken unless you actually wait for something to appear. - **Prefer a ref over a selector.** A selector that silently matches nothing and an element that is genuinely absent produce the same failure, and you cannot tell them apart without looking. `--snapshot` first, then act on what it listed. When a check still says something is missing, use `--snapshot --full` to read the tree before reporting it, and screenshot if the question is genuinely visual. - Third-party analytics failures are filtered out; they are noise, not signal. ## One run, one browser (the default) By default each invocation launches a browser, does the work, and closes it. Cookies, logins and page state do **not** survive to the next invocation, so a short sequence should happen inside a single `--script` run rather than across several calls. This is the right default: most QA is "load this, tell me what broke." ## Sessions — keep one page alive across calls When you need to *think between steps* — drive a form, read the result, decide the next action, drive again — a single `--script` can't help, because you don't know step 3 until you've seen step 2. Use `--session `: the browser stays alive between separate invocations and every call reconnects to the **same page** it left open. ```bash # Step 1: open the app in a named session, set something up node /browser.mjs http://localhost:3000 --session qa1 --snapshot # Step 2: NO url — act on the page the session already has open node /browser.mjs --session qa1 --eval "document.querySelector('#total').innerText" # Step 3: re-navigate within the same session if you want, or keep acting node /browser.mjs --session qa1 --script ./next-step.mjs # When done — always tear it down, or the browser stays running node /browser.mjs --session qa1 --close ``` Rules: - **Omit the url** on follow-up calls to act on the current page; **pass a url** to navigate the session's page somewhere new. - Refs from `--snapshot` still die on navigation/re-render — re-snapshot after anything that changes the page, same as one-shot mode. - **Always `--close` when finished.** The browser is detached and outlives the call by design; without `--close` it keeps running until the machine reboots. - Sessions are headless and use a throwaway profile per id under `~/.codegpt/ab-sessions/` — never the user's real browser or cookies. ## Notes - Resolves `patchright` from an installed CodeGPT extension, then a dev checkout, then a global copy — so it normally needs no install of its own. If none is found it says what it looked for. - Headless. It never touches the user's real browser profile or cookies. **`TRASH/preview-screening-requirements-panel.html`** — open it in your browser. There's a **BEFORE / AFTER** toggle at the top.

## What it does

**AFTER tab** is fully interactive — switch positions, add skills, remove them, publish.

- **Pick a position** → its requirement template resolves and the skills/certs appear as chips automatically
- **Chips** show live `✓` recognised / `◌` to-review, using the same vocabulary the screener matches against
- **`+`** on a grey chip adds that term to the reference data
- **`+ Add skill`** is a combobox over the vocabulary — so you can't type a skill that won't match

- **Confirm dialog** appears when you switch position on a post that already has requirements, and shows exactly what will be added and removed
- A position with **no template** shows an empty state with "Create requirements for this position", and **keeps** whatever skills were already on the post instead of silently wiping them

Let me be concrete and useful. The core problem: users end up putting skills content into Responsibilities/Qualifications because the Required Skills textarea is a blank slate.

Alternatives worth considering:

**Alternative 1: Don't add a new panel — make Responsibilities/Qualifications themselves entity-aware.**
Keep exactly the blocks they have, but run every line through the entity analyzer live. As HR types into Responsibilities, lines that match the skills vocabulary get tagged "this is a skill" with a one-click "move to Required Skills" action. So skills get *extracted* from where they naturally land rather than being asked for in a separate box.
- Pro: zero new UI, no new block, HR never thinks about skills.

**Alternative 2: Merge skills into Qualifications, drop the separate block entirely.**
One "Qualifications & Requirements" block. Lines are auto-classified into skill vs cert vs education by the existing regex + vocabulary. `skills_json` is derived at save time from the classified lines.
- Pro: reduces 3 boxes → 2, which is the real complaint.
- Con: needs a classifier at save time; risks polluting required_skills with sentences. Needs a new save-time derivation step.

**Alternative 3: Position-first wizard instead of a drag-and-drop canvas.**
Rather than a block on the canvas, make the builder a short guided flow: 1) pick position 2) requirements auto-load (read-only, from template) 3) write the prose (AI-assisted) 4) publish. Just replace the textarea with a multi-select combobox writing to `draft.skills`. No auto-apply, no education/experience move, no gate change.

/**
     * Vocab-preferred prompt: the model must reuse vocabulary terms verbatim
     * for skills (and certifications inside qualifications) and may introduce
     * at most 2 new terms when nothing fits.
     */
    protected function buildPrompt(array $job, array $vocabulary): string
    {
        $skills = array_values(array_unique(array_filter(array_map('trim', $vocabulary['skills'] ?? []))));
        $certs = array_values(array_unique(array_filter(array_map('trim', $vocabulary['certifications'] ?? []))));

        // Keep the prompt bounded: most hotel vocabularies fit, but cap anyway.
        $skills = array_slice($skills, 0, 150);
        $certs = array_slice($certs, 0, 60);

        $lines = [
            'You are an HR copywriter for Oxford Suites Makati, a premier all-suite hotel in Makati\'s business district known for warm Filipino hospitality.',
            'Write a job-post draft for this role. Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly these keys: description, responsibilities, qualifications, skills, instructions, about.',
            '',
            'Role context:',
            '- Position: ' . ($job['position_title'] ?? 'Staff'),
            '- Department: ' . ($job['department'] ?? 'General'),
            '- Employment type: ' . ($job['employment_type'] ?? 'Full-time'),
            '- Schedule: ' . ($job['schedule'] ?? 'Shifting Schedule'),
            '- Vacancies: ' . ($job['vacancies'] ?? 1),
            '- Experience level: ' . ($job['experience_level'] ?? 'Not specified'),
            '- Education level: ' . ($job['education_level'] ?? 'Not specified'),
            '',
            'Screening vocabulary (terms the applicant-screening model recognizes):',
            '- SKILLS: ' . ($skills ? implode('; ', $skills) : '(none)'),
            '- CERTIFICATIONS: ' . ($certs ? implode('; ', $certs) : '(none)'),
            '',
            'Rules:',
            '1. description: 2-3 sentences pitching the role at Oxford Suites Makati.',
            '2. responsibilities: 5-7 bullets, each under 120 characters, plain text, no numbering.',
            '3. qualifications: 4-6 bullets; mention a CERTIFICATION from the list above when relevant (e.g. TESDA NC II, Food Handler).',
            '4. skills: 6-10 items; PREFER the SKILLS vocabulary verbatim (exact spelling). You may add at most 2 new terms only when nothing in the list fits.',
            '5. instructions: 1-2 sentences telling applicants to send their updated resume through the posting or walk in at the HR Office, Oxford Suites Makati.',
            '6. about: 1-2 sentences about Oxford Suites Makati as a premier all-suite hotel in Makati.',
            '7. Keep language professional, hotel-appropriate, Philippine English. No markdown, no numbering, no extra keys.',
        ];

        return implode("\n", $lines);
    }

content.text: Analyzing causes of perceived slowness from large file size, repeated edits, and tool checks, and framing mitigation options.

It's slow for three concrete reasons:

1. **That one file is huge** — `RecruitmentManagement.tsx` is ~7,000 lines. Every edit + `tsc --noEmit` re-checks the whole frontend, and most of the errors it reports are pre-existing, not ours.

2. **My verification loop is heavy** — full `tsc`, `php -l` on every file, plus browser automation runs that sometimes take 30s to load. That's my process being thorough, not your app.

3. **The app itself has slow paths:**
   - AI generation walks Groq → OpenRouter → Gemini with retries and a 30s timeout per provider
   - The vocabulary + scoring config fetch on builder open adds API round-trips
   - A 7k-line component re-renders a lot on every keystroke

If you mean the **UI feels slow**, tell me where — builder typing, position switch, Generate with AI, or publish — and I'll profile that spot.

If you mean **my implementation pace**, I can switch to smaller batches: finish the panel + gate first, verify once, then do the AI modal last. Want me to do that?

Done. The preview is now your real Job Post Builder. Here's what changed:

## Backend (all `php -l` clean, tests pass)
- **New migration** `2026_10_13_000001_add_additional_instructions_about_to_job_posts_table.php` — adds `additional_json` (JSON), `instructions` + `about` (text), all nullable. No columns or tables removed.
- `JobPost.php` — the three fields added to `$fillable` + `additional_json` cast to `array`.
- `StoreJobPostRequest` / `UpdateJobPostRequest` — `'additional' => ['nullable','array']`, `'instructions'/'about' => ['nullable','string']`.
- `RecruitmentManagementController` — `store()` maps `additional` → `additional_json`; `update()` mirrors it; `generateDraft()` accepts `blocks[]` + `notes{}`, passes them plus `experience_level`/`education_level` to the generator, and the grounding report now scans generated prose for vocabulary terms (skills are no longer generated).
- `JobContentGenerator::buildPrompt` — generates **only the ticked blocks**, honours each block's note, and no longer asks for a `skills` key. `normalize()` handles `additional`.
- Both `JobPostResource`s (Recruitment + Landing) expose the three new fields.

## Frontend
- **Screening Requirements panel** replaces the Required Skills textarea (`RecruitmentManagement.tsx`): Position picker on top (drives the template), template banner, Skills as vocabulary chips with ✓/+/✕ and a combobox, Certifications derived read-only from Qualifications, Education/Experience shown read-only (they stay editable in Job Info, per your call).
- **Additional Info** block below Qualifications, persisted end-to-end.
- **Instructions + About now persist** — they were silently dropped before; saved posts reload them instead of resetting to defaults.
- **Position auto-apply** with confirm-before-overwrite dialog (shows +will add / −will remove).
- **Publish gate** requires all six prose blocks *plus* ≥1 recognised skill (falls back to any skill line if the vocabulary hasn't loaded).
- **Generate with AI is now a modal**: read-only context (Position, Department, Skills, Certificate, Education, Experience) + the six checkboxes `Job Description, Key Responsibilities, Qualifications, Additional Info, Application Instruction, About Company`, each with its own notes box. Prose blocks replace, bullet blocks merge without duplicating; report shows reused vocabulary terms.
- Public job page renders Additional Info, How to Apply, and About Company sections.

## Verification
- `php -l` clean on all six backend files + migration.
- `tsc --noEmit`: only the pre-existing `FileCheck` error remains — nothing new.
- `JobContentGeneratorTest`: 9/9 pass. `ScreeningRequirementTemplateTest`: 2/2 pass.

## Two things to know
1. **Run the migration** (`php artisan migrate`) — until then, saving Additional Info/Instructions/About will fail validation at the DB layer.
2. I did **not** commit anything — the tree already had unrelated uncommitted work, and this repo syncs to Lovable. Say the word if you want a commit, and tell me whether to include only these files.

Removed the local remnants. Now the important part — what that does and doesn't do.

## Why I mentioned it

`frontend/AGENTS.md` contained a Lovable notice instructing any agent working in this repo not to rewrite pushed git history, because pushes to the connected branch sync back into the Lovable editor. That's the only reason I brought it up.

## What I just removed

- `frontend/AGENTS.md` — the file was *only* that notice (10 lines, nothing else), so I deleted the file.
- `frontend/src/lib/lovable-error-reporting.ts` — dead code, imported nowhere. Verified zero references before deleting.

I left alone: the `README.md` mentions (docs text only), the `bunfig.toml` package excludes (harmless), and the stale `bun.lock` entries (not the live lockfile — `package-lock.json` is, and it has no Lovable packages). Your `package.json` and `vite.config.ts` have zero Lovable dependencies, so the build never touched it.

## What this does NOT do

The actual sync is server-side: **Lovable dashboard ↔ your GitHub repo** (`Franzwll/2nd-repo-for-hrms-backend-`). Deleting local files cannot break that connection — pushing to the connected branch will still show up in the Lovable editor.

To fully disconnect, you have to do it where the connection lives (needs your login, I can't do it from here):

1. In Lovable: project → **Settings → GitHub → Disconnect** (or remove the project).
2. In GitHub: **Settings → Applications → Lovable → Revoke**, if you want it fully gone.

Once that's done, the history-rewrite caution no longer applies and you're free to rebase/squash normally.
